s: The term ‘tsunami’ is derived from which combination of Japanese words and meanings?
x: In Japanese, ‘tsu’ means harbour and ‘nami’ means wave; hence tsunami literally means ‘harbour wave’.

s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes a tsunami from a tidal wave?
o: A tsunami results from sudden displacement of the ocean floor, whereas tides result mainly from gravitational pull.
A tsunami consists of a single wave, whereas tides always consist of multiple waves.
A tsunami is confined to shallow water, whereas tides occur only in deep oceans.
A tsunami is caused by gravitational attraction, whereas a tidal wave is caused by earthquakes.
x: Tsunamis are generated by sudden displacement of the ocean floor, usually due to tectonic activity. Tides are produced mainly by the gravitational pull of the Moon and the Sun.
tq: Separate two commonly confused terms by matching each with its actual cause.

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the causes of tsunamis:
1. Subduction-related undersea earthquakes are the chief cause of tsunamis.
2. Submarine landslides and volcanic eruptions can also generate tsunamis.
3. Asteroid or meteorite impacts in the ocean can produce tsunamis.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. Tsunamis may result from tectonic earthquakes, submarine landslides, volcanic eruptions and large asteroid or meteorite impacts.
tq: Use the inclusive option after checking whether every listed triggering mechanism is supported.

s: Which of the following combinations regarding tsunami behaviour is correctly matched?

Deep ocean—long wavelength and low wave height
Deep ocean—short wavelength and very high wave height
Near coast—high speed and barely noticeable waves
x: In the deep ocean, a tsunami has a very long wavelength, low height and high speed. Its height increases considerably near the coast as it enters shallow water.
tq: Compare the same phenomenon in two settings and identify the correct paired characteristics.

s: A tsunami travelling through the deep ocean may attain a speed of approximately:

The wave loses all its energy through evaporation.

x: As a tsunami enters shallow coastal water, its speed decreases and its wave height rises sharply, producing severe inundation.
